analyst_view.overall: Early view: Sassuolo should be under a new coach by now after Aquilani was sacked; several reports say Roberto D'Aversa has been chosen. Allegri's Napoli are tenth after a poor run and come into this five days after a Champions League trip to Manchester City; Allegri has been backed by the club, but one report describes tension around Napoli. Badiashile, out for about a month from late October, could be back.

goals.text: The numbers say 3.1 goals. Sassuolo's home games have produced almost five goals a game, but a new coach usually makes his side tighter, and Napoli's away games have averaged about 2.8. Those pull in opposite directions, so I stay with the number.

corners.text: The site expects 9.1 corners. I lean higher: Napoli's away games have averaged about 11 corners, because they rely on crosses when their build-up stalls, as it did against Lazio. Sassuolo concede about six corners a game.

cards.text: The numbers say 3.4 cards. Napoli's games are among the calmest in the league at about 2.7 cards, but Sassuolo's home games have averaged about four, and a struggling side under a new coach tends to play with more intensity. I stay with the number.

shots.text: The site expects 26.3 shots. I lean higher because Napoli's away games have averaged almost 32 shots, with both sides shooting freely. Sassuolo allow almost 17 shots a game, and they will have to come out at home.

shots_on_target.text: The numbers say 9.3 shots on target. Sassuolo concede more shots on target than anyone, but Napoli's finishing has been poor lately and the new coach should make Sassuolo harder to get through, so I stay with the number.
